subsystems.name: Power stage
subsystems.role: switches the DC link into a controlled AC waveform.

subsystems.name: Output filter
subsystems.role: smooths switching ripple into a clean sine wave.

subsystems.name: Control processor
subsystems.role: runs the grid-forming loop fast enough to react within milliseconds.

subsystems.name: Grid-forming control law
subsystems.role: synthesises an internal voltage phasor instead of following the grid.
parts: droop or virtual synchronous machine loop

subsystems.name: Energy source
subsystems.role: supplies the DC side of the inverter.
parts: wind or solar converter with power headroom

subsystems.name: Plant controller
subsystems.role: coordinates many inverters so a whole farm behaves like one machine.

buildSteps.title: Choose the control law
buildSteps.detail: Designers pick droop control, a virtual synchronous machine model, or virtual oscillator control, then tune virtual inertia and impedance against simulations of the target grid.

buildSteps.title: Size the semiconductors
buildSteps.detail: Modules are chosen for continuous current plus overload margins, since an inverter can only push roughly 1.1–1.5 times rated current during a fault, far below a spinning generator's 5–6 times.

buildSteps.title: Build the power stack
buildSteps.detail: Modules, DC-link capacitors, busbars and cooling are assembled into a cabinet with low-inductance connections.

buildSteps.title: Fit the filter and protection
buildSteps.detail: LCL filters, contactors and relays are installed and the resonant behaviour of filter and grid is checked.

buildSteps.title: Write and flash the firmware
buildSteps.detail: The control loop runs at tens of microseconds; current limiting, anti-islanding and ride-through logic are coded and documented.

buildSteps.title: Hardware-in-the-loop test
buildSteps.detail: The real controller is driven against a simulated grid, including weak-grid, fault and islanding scenarios, before it ever touches a live network.

buildSteps.title: Type-test to grid codes
buildSteps.detail: The unit is certified for fault ride-through, frequency response, harmonics and, where required, black-start capability.

buildSteps.title: Commission on site
buildSteps.detail: Engineers verify it holds voltage and frequency stably on a weak feeder, then step it up to parallel operation with many units.

prerequisites.tech: Fast power semiconductors and digital control
prerequisites.why: the control loop must respond in milliseconds; silicon-carbide devices and FPGAs make that practical.
a grid-forming inverter needs energy to push or absorb when it props up frequency.
most standards still define grid-following performance; grid-forming requirements are only now being written.
planners cannot approve thousands of units they cannot confidently model in stability studies.
proof has so far come from islands and isolated networks, not large interconnected systems.

pathway.milestone: grid-forming batteries in island and weak-grid systems, plus virtual-inertia modes on large storage (for example in South Australia)
pathway.unlocks: evidence that power electronics can hold frequency without rotating machines.

pathway.milestone: grid codes and certification tests that define grid-forming performance
pathway.unlocks: procurement at scale, with planners able to rely on the behaviour.

pathway.milestone: plant-level and fleet-level grid-forming, including black start from renewables
pathway.unlocks: restoring a grid after a blackout without fossil generators.

pathway.milestone: high-renewable grids run mostly on inverter-based resources
pathway.unlocks: power systems that stay stable with little or no synchronous generation.
